## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

⚠️ **Gate recommendation: approve with a non-blocking risk.**

The observed-key union preserves later fields in ordinary dictionary writes and keeps columns omitted from the whole batch absent for partial merge updates. Local add, create, merge, and boundary checks pass.

Blob rows retain the existing field-loss limitation. [#4485](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4485) is an earlier open fix for the same issue that also covers blob conversion; coordinate which implementation lands.

review_comments.body:
Rows with blob fields still bypass the new helper, so an ordinary field first supplied in a later row is silently lost. `_blob_input_to_arrow` builds its table with `pa.Table.from_pylist(rows)` before returning here; the ordinary `add` path also calls that conversion first. This behavior is unchanged from the base, but those inputs do not receive this fix.

Including the nullable key in the first row (with `None` if needed) avoids the loss. The shared conversion in [#4485](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4485) covers this path as well.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```python
import lancedb
import pyarrow as pa

db = lancedb.connect("memory://")
schema = pa.schema([
    pa.field("id", pa.int64()),
    pa.field("note", pa.string()),
    lancedb.blob("payload"),
])
table = db.create_table("example", schema=schema)
table.add([
    {"id": 1, "payload": b"a"},
    {"id": 2, "payload": b"b", "note": "keep me"},
])
assert table.to_arrow()["note"].to_pylist() == [None, "keep me"]
# Observed on this head: [None, None]
```

</details>
